articles.title: Has anybody seen my keys? A key-hierarchy strategy for rack-level security
articles.summary: A key-hierarchy strategy for rack-level security involves using Shamir secret sharing to protect storage at rest and sprockets sessions for application layer messages. This is achieved by splitting a shared rack-level secret into N unique key shares, distributing them over sprockets sessions to each bootstrap agent, and verifying membership in the group using exchanged public key certificates. This ensures that an attacker cannot walk off with a subset of sleds or drives and recover any useful information, providing rack-level security guarantees.

articles.title: Mmuko Boot Sequence – a tiny freestanding C kernel that boots in QEMU
articles.summary: MMUKO Boot Sequence is a tiny freestanding C kernel that boots in QEMU, allowing it to run independently of a host operating system. This is achieved by using a freestanding MMUKO program, which uses printf, malloc, calloc, and the host OS C runtime. This kernel is designed to support two boot paths: direct BIOS boot and GRUB multiboot. The direct boot path uses a 512-byte BIOS boot sector, loads a 512-byte kernel flat-kernel, and switches to 32-bit protected mode. The GRUB path uses GRUB Multiboot as the loader, initializes screen and serial output, and runs the MMUKO boot phases. This allows MMUKO to boot in QEMU without requiring a host operating system.
